result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use transaction, ad-hoc or compensation behavior only when its specific semantics are explicitly described.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

result.rule: When the description explicitly identifies a substantive verification as part of a broader review: Model the verification as a BPMN activity rather than leaving it implicit in the broader review.
When the description lists multiple distinct evaluation objectives within an assessment.: Model each objective as a separate BPMN activity rather than combining them into one activity.

When the description states an activity and separately specifies criteria used to perform it: Label the activity with its concise core action; do not add the criteria to the activity label unless they are needed to distinguish it from another activity.

When the description states that information is reported or submitted and separately says it is later entered or recorded in a system: Model the reporting or submission and the later system-recording work as separate BPMN elements; do not treat the initial report as completing the recording activity.

args.text: When a process description states the condition that starts or ends the process, label the corresponding start or end event with that condition rather than a generic label such as start or end. Use task labels that preserve the actions and objects stated in the description.

trace.reason: Check existing guidance relevant to semantic faithfulness and event/task labels before proposing a guideline.

result.rule: Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.

result.rule: When the description explicitly states the outcome that ends the process: Label the BPMN end event with a concise phrase that preserves that stated outcome rather than using a generic label.

When the description names an activity or milestone for which a BPMN task is being labeled: Label the task to preserve the action and purpose stated in the description; do not substitute a related but different action or milestone.
